explain.say: Do you have pepper at home? About 600 years ago in Europe, pepper and other spices were costly treasures. That is one reason European sailors risked their lives on unknown oceans. The board shows the main reasons, one by one.

faq.a: Spices like pepper, cloves and nutmeg flavoured food and were used in medicine. They grew only in faraway places like India and the Maluku Islands, so they were rare and costly in Europe.

faq.q: Why did Europeans want to avoid the old routes?
faq.a: Spices passed through many traders, including Arab, Venetian and Ottoman-area merchants, each adding a profit. A direct sea route meant cheaper spices and bigger profits for European kingdoms.
asks: Why not use the land routes?

faq.a: A small, fast Portuguese ship of the 1400s with triangular lateen sails, which let it sail closer into the wind. It was ideal for exploring coasts.

faq.q: How did sailors find their way?
faq.a: They used a magnetic compass for direction and an astrolabe or quadrant to measure the height of the Sun or stars, which told them how far north or south they were.

faq.q: What does gold, God and glory mean?
faq.a: It is a short way to remember explorers' motives: wealth, spreading Christianity, and fame for themselves and their rulers. Historians add others, like curiosity and rivalry between kingdoms.

facts: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in India in 1498.
Magellan's expedition, completed under Juan Sebastian Elcano in 1522, was the first to sail around the world.
Zheng He's fleets made seven voyages between 1405 and 1433.
